properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued August 15 at 9:00PM MDT by NWS Pueblo CO
properties.description:
At 900 PM MDT, Doppler radar was tracking a strong thunderstorm 12
miles north of Brandon, or 15 miles southwest of Cheyenne Wells,
moving east at 10 mph.

HAZARD...Wind gusts up to 50 mph and nickel size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around
unsecured objects. Minor hail damage to vegetation is
possible.

This storm will remain over mainly rural areas of northeastern Kiowa
County.

properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued August 15 at 8:21PM MDT until August 15 at 9:30PM MDT by NWS Denver CO
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Phillips County in northeastern Colorado...
Southeastern Sedgwick County in northeastern Colorado...
Northeastern Washington County in northeastern Colorado...

* WHEN...Until 930 PM MDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...

- At 819 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain was moving
out of the Advisory area. Minor flooding is ongoing or expected
to begin shortly in the advisory area. Between 0.5 and 2 inches
of rain have fallen.

- Flooding impacts will continue, but no additional rainfall is
expected.

- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Holyoke, Haxtun, Otis, Paoli, Highland Center, Fairfield, Lone
Star, Sixteen-Mile Corner, Amherst, Pleasant Valley, Burdett,
Platner and Hyde.
properties.areaDesc: Phillips, CO; Sedgwick, CO; Washington, CO

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued August 15 at 8:13PM MDT until August 15 at 10:15PM MDT by NWS Denver CO
properties.description:
At 813 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing heavy
rain were moving out of the warned area. Between 2 and 4 inches of
rain have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts up to 0.2 inches are
possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to
begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, gulches, roads,
and poor drainage and low-lying areas.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Mainly rural areas of Southeastern Lincoln County.

This includes the following streams and drainages...
Rush Creek, South Rush Creek and Adobe Creek.

properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued August 15 at 8:09PM MDT until August 16 at 9:00AM MDT by NWS Denver CO
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...North Central Adams County in northeastern Colorado...
Southwestern Morgan County in northeastern Colorado...

* WHEN...Until 900 AM MDT Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in rural and low-lying areas along Bijou
creek from central Adams through southwestern Morgan counties.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...

- At 809 PM MDT, Local law enforcement reported flooding had
occurred along Bijou Creek through Adams County. Water had caused
closer of a couple county roads, but they have since reopened.
Water had also crested and spilled onto Colfax Avenue in rural
Adams County. The crest has passed this area, but will continue
moving downstream and affect areas farther north through the Hoyt
area and toward the confluence with the South Platte River in
Morgan County.

- This includes the following streams and drainages...
Bijou Creek.

- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
rural and low lying areas along Bijou Creek.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued August 15 at 7:52PM MDT until August 15 at 10:00PM MDT by NWS Pueblo CO
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Portions of central, east central, and southeast Colorado,
including the following areas, Teller, El Paso, Huerfano, Las
Animas, Crowley, Otero, Kiowa, Bent and Prowers Counties.

* WHEN...Until 10 PM MDT this evening.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Abundant monsoon moisture will result in scattered to numerous
thunderstorms this afternoon and evening which will be capable of
producing heavy rainfall and flash flooding, especially for urban
areas or locations with already saturated soil conditions.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued August 15 at 11:32AM MDT until August 16 at 6:00AM MDT by NWS Goodland KS
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...Portions of east central Colorado, including the following
area, Cheyenne CO and west central Kansas, including the following
areas, Gove, Greeley, Logan, Wallace and Wichita.

* WHEN...From 6 PM MDT  /7 PM CDT/ this evening through late tonight.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Low-water crossings may be flooded.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- 1-3 inches of rain the past couple nights along with the
potential for another cluster or two of storms this evening and
overnight increases the potential for some flooding and even
flash flooding. Rainfall rates of 1.5 to 2.5 inches per hour is
possible in the strongest cells.
